status: fictional explanatory scenario, not a real mission or certified spacecraft design

timeline.chapters_0_to_19: Founding-era Lyra as a child, usually age eight in illustrations; parents Amina and Jonas alive. Technical examples are conceptual, not a calendar of separate disasters.
timeline.chapters_20_to_21: Adult Lyra about thirty-five; teaches and helps maintain community.
timeline.chapter_22: Elderly Lyra about seventy-five passes notebook to archive; natural death, no resurrection.
timeline.chapter_23: Centuries and many generations later: Sera age eight, a distinct descendant of the community. Not Lyra, not merely her next-age version.
timeline.chapters_24_to_30: Adult Sera about thirty-five in late-voyage/approach frame; concept comparisons in chapter 30 are not available technologies.
timeline.chapter_31: Mature Sera about forty-five considers future choices near target star; no guaranteed safe landing.

characters.Lyra: medium-brown skin; TWO curly hair buns; teal/orange clothing; cream CIRCLE patch; gray hair and wrinkles when elderly
characters.Amina: adult Black mother, low tied braids; mustard coveralls and teal belt; founding era only
characters.Jonas: adult East Asian father, straight short black hair; navy coveralls/red collar; founding era only
characters.Sera: medium-brown skin; ONE long SINGLE BRAID; copper-red jacket and teal shirt; cream TRIANGLE patch; child/adult/mature stages; not living beside founders

ship_visuals: two coaxial ring habitats separated along long nonrotating central spine
rounded leading shield at nose, aft engine at other end, radiator fins on aft spine
coasting exterior has no continuous engine plume, warp trails or asteroid fields
interior recurrent locations: garden, green bench with orange repair patches, classroom, workshop, clinic, communications room
apparent down in rotating ring points outward toward rim; no gravity generator
schematics and scale are illustrative, not structural or medical validation
science_limits: fictional nearby candidate habitat, not announced second Earth or confirmed safe Proxima b
illustrative cruise arithmetic is not an integrated trajectory or propulsion design
no universal safe shielding thickness, minimum crew number, proven multi-generation reproductive safety or perfect closed ecology
late Earth pictures are archives/monitors, not a giant Earth outside the centuries-later window
descendants have agency; reproductive model assumptions are not endorsed coercive policy
robotic probes, lightsails, hibernation and embryo concepts have distinct unsolved problems; no working passenger service asserted
